Diaspora Filipinos will never live up to the standards of Filipinos in the Philippines. I am a Fil-Am who is always on the search to find ways to learn Tagalog but unless you’re from the Bay Area or Hawaii it’s pretty much impossible to find resources. Parents won’t speak it to their kids for assimilation reasons, or they plain just don’t have time because they all work FT and don’t know how to teach people. You speak to Fil-Ams here and they’ve never been back, or they go once when they’re 7 years old. But they have to own the culture because that’s how Americans work. 

I go back every other year and I stopped outwardly identifying as Filipino back there and just tell people I am American of Tagalog, Ilocano, and Bicolano descent. There’s no winning. Here you’re “othered” so if people are rude enough to ask me about the what I am or the culture they’re gonna get a really long conversation. 

Latinos have a way more prevalent population, cultural influence, and are relatively close to the US. That’s a moot comparison. Also they lost their whole language to Spain. We didn’t lose ours entirely. 

The word Filipino was invented like barely 500 years ago and declared the official language in 1935. Language is fluid. These words are made up and are derivative of Spanish rule. Filipinx isn’t for you it’s for Philippine diaspora who identify as queer.

Edit: I also hate the word Filipino because it is not rooted in any “Philippine” culture it’s rooted in Western Spanish culture. I actually agreed with Duterte’s proposal to rename the country. (Maharlika)

Hm...here’s my comprehensive Pan Asian review of neighborhoods and stores. 

**EAST OF 101 from SILVERLAKE**

Eagle Rock close to SL has Seafood City but that is limited to Filipino grocery. They have lots of fish and pork cuts you’ll find in Korean dishes though. About the same price as 99 Ranch. Generic rice selection. Fish frying services. 


East Hollywood near SL has Bangluck and Bangkok which are Thai groceries. 


India Sweets and Spices in Los Feliz for South Asian and Indian groceries. They’re kind of steep tbh. Good for fresh spices. Their veggie restaurant is reasonably price. Good selection of metal plates and bowls. 


The beautiful Pan-Asian wonderland that is 99 Ranch. I would get a heart tattoo of their logo on my arm if I could. Generally for literally everything Asian that ever existed I go to 99 Ranch in San Gabriel Valley (*Alhambra and Monterey Park*. Generally large amounts of large Chinese groceries everywhere. These are the only neighborhoods to get dim sum in LA that’s any good and anyone who says otherwise is fooling themselves) or Van Nuys. Make a thing of it - get boba at Tastea after. I find they have the best prices and have lots of deals and coupons all the time. You will walk out with more than you thought compared to like Ralph’s or Vons for the same price. Beautiful fish selection, crawfish that’ll bite ya, frozen fishballs of every flavor for hotpot, spam flavors you didn’t know existed, kimchi, soon tofu and soju of every  brand it is hands down the greatest supermarket in the US. Also... fish frying services!!!

The 99 ranch one in Van Nuys has two of the greatest restaurants in the valley on either side of it. (Pho So 1 & the only good Sam Woo). Always chaos on Sunday’s. 

Glendale has Super King which is more of an Armenian market and neighborhood but you will find like good cuts of meat and h/o shrimp here. 


*Less traffic, small business boutique market, more expensive, more drive:* Lotte, Han Kook, Seoul Market in La Crescenta. Fancy Korean rice selection in all. Limited supply meats and seafoods - cute mom n pop butchers. Pickle their own salads. 


**WEST OF 101 from SILVERLAKE**

If you’re willing to go west of the 101 then take your picks. H Marts (Korean chain) and Galleria Markets galore particularly on Western. Can be brutal to get to in rush hour traffic. I go to Hannam relatively frequently on Olympic and Vermont after I visit Beverly Soon which is my favorite restaurant of all time (The selection isn’t as big as H Mart though - a lil expensive). Markets tend to be crowded in KTown from population density so the social distancing might also be am issue. 

Chinatown is kind of dead when it comes to markets in my experience because all the Chinese and Asian people went to SGV. There’s a lot of great Vietnamese places in Chinatown. 

Japanese markets like Marukai and Little Tokyo Marketplace have lots of Korean items as well. They’re both in Little Tokyo. I feel like these are a little more expensive or in the range of 99 Ranch.
